sections.title: Why mc-novatools.com was built
body: MC NovaTools was built after repeated everyday friction: a user needs to merge a PDF before sending a client packet, compress an image before publishing a page, format JSON before debugging an API response, estimate a mortgage refinance break-even point, or convert text without installing a heavy desktop application. Many utility websites solve those problems with a single input box, but they often leave users unsure about privacy, assumptions, limitations, and what to verify before trusting the result. This site was created to make the tool and the review process visible together.

The project focuses on browser-based processing wherever practical. PDF and image tasks are designed around local browser APIs and client-side libraries so documents and working files do not need to be intentionally uploaded to MC NovaTools for ordinary use. Developer tools such as formatters, encoders, validators, diff checkers, and checksum helpers are written for fast in-page work. Finance calculators emphasize transparent inputs, clear assumptions, and explicit disclaimers instead of pretending that an estimate is advice. The result is a utility platform for preparation, review, and handoff rather than a black-box decision engine.

MC NovaTools is intentionally broad because real workflows are broad. A small business preparing tax records may need PDF cleanup, image resizing, CSV inspection, text cleanup, a calculator, and a naming checklist in the same afternoon. A developer reviewing a support issue may need URL encoding, JSON formatting, Base64 conversion, and a screenshot-size reduction workflow. Bringing these tools together reduces context switching while keeping each tool focused on a specific job.

sections.title: Mission and operating principles
body: The mission is to provide fast, understandable, privacy-conscious browser tools with enough context for users to know what the output can and cannot do. MC NovaTools is not trying to replace professional judgment, accounting advice, legal review, security review, or accessibility testing. It helps users prepare better inputs, catch common mistakes, and document assumptions before a result is shared.

The editorial standard is simple: every public page should explain what the tool does, what inputs are expected, how output should be reviewed, and when a human expert should be involved. Pages should avoid fake ratings, unverifiable claims, inflated traffic numbers, and vague marketing language. If a tool runs locally, the copy says so carefully. If a workflow may involve third-party services such as Google Analytics, Google AdSense, advertising cookies, live reference data, or external links, the privacy and disclaimer pages explain that boundary.

In practice, that means a page is not considered complete just because a button works. A complete MC NovaTools page should help a user decide whether the tool is appropriate, prepare a safe copy of the input, understand what the browser is doing, review the result, and know when to stop and ask for specialized help. This product philosophy is especially important for PDF, image, finance, and developer utilities because a technically valid output can still be wrong for the user’s real destination.

sections.title: Team and review roles
body: MC NovaTools is maintained as a small, remote-first project. The current public editorial lead is Metehan Çetin, LPC, who reviews site content for practical clarity, privacy-first language, accessibility concerns, finance disclaimers, and user-facing workflow quality. The project also uses a named editorial role for routine content review so readers can separate authorship from quality control. Public profiles are linked where available, and author pages explain areas of knowledge, review scope, and limitations.

sections.title: Experience and expertise behind the tools
body: The site’s expertise is practical and implementation-focused. File utilities are evaluated around common browser constraints such as memory usage, file size, page ordering, metadata risk, output naming, and the importance of keeping an original copy. Image tools are reviewed around compression trade-offs, transparent backgrounds, resizing for email or social platforms, and the difference between preparation and final production design. Developer utilities are reviewed around encoding safety, formatting correctness, validation limits, and not pasting secrets into convenience tools.

Finance tools receive additional caution. Calculators can make assumptions easier to compare, but they cannot know a user’s complete tax situation, credit profile, local rules, lender terms, investment risk tolerance, or future market conditions. MC NovaTools therefore treats finance outputs as educational estimates and asks users to verify important decisions with qualified professionals. This is part of the trust model, not a footnote.

The experience behind MC NovaTools is therefore not presented as a claim that every professional domain is solved by one website. It is presented as applied web-product experience: building and reviewing small tools, writing cautious instructions, protecting route stability, checking metadata, avoiding unnecessary uploads, and making quality-control steps visible. That is the expertise users need from a utility platform before they decide whether a result is ready to use.

sections.title: Response-time promise
body: We aim to acknowledge support and correction messages within two business days. Privacy rights requests, security reports, broken route reports, and finance-tool accuracy concerns receive priority because they can affect trust and user safety. Complex requests may take longer if they require reproducing a bug, checking a browser-specific issue, or reviewing copy across multiple localized pages.

When reporting a bug, include the page URL, browser, device type, a short description of the input format, the expected result, and the actual result. For privacy, send a small synthetic example instead of real personal documents whenever possible. For finance calculators, include the assumptions you entered, but do not send bank logins, account numbers, Social Security numbers, tax IDs, or private statements.

Business inquiries are welcome when they are relevant to privacy-first utilities, accessibility, localization, educational content, or responsible advertising. We do not accept proposals that require hidden tracking, deceptive ad placement, scraped user data, fake testimonials, paid reviews without disclosure, or claims that cannot be verified. Tool requests are prioritized when they fit the existing client-side architecture, solve a repeatable user problem, and can be explained with clear limits.

Security reports should include only the minimum information needed to reproduce the concern. If you believe a page exposes private data, creates an unsafe download, weakens consent behavior, or links to a misleading destination, mark the subject line as “Security” or “Privacy” so it can be triaged ahead of general feature requests. sections.title: General tool accuracy disclaimer
body: MC NovaTools provides browser-based utilities and written guides for practical preparation work. The tools can help merge, split, inspect, format, convert, calculate, compress, rename, compare, and organize information, but they cannot guarantee that every input is complete, every file is valid, every assumption is correct, or every output is suitable for a final decision. Results may vary by browser, device memory, file structure, encoding, locale, third-party library behavior, user settings, and the quality of the original source.

Always keep the original file or source data. Review page order, formatting, metadata, units, dates, filenames, special characters, rounding, and edge-case warnings before using an output. If a result affects money, taxes, legal obligations, compliance, accessibility, security, publishing, client delivery, or official records, obtain a qualified human review.

A tool may appear to complete successfully while still requiring review. For example, a PDF merge can preserve pages but not the business meaning of their order; an image compressor can reduce size but damage text legibility; a JSON formatter can make syntax readable without proving the API response is semantically correct; and a text converter can change characters in ways that matter for legal names, product codes, or URLs. Treat the output as prepared material, not automatic approval.

sections.title: Finance and calculator disclaimers
body: Finance calculators on MC NovaTools are educational estimation tools. Mortgage, refinance, compound interest, retirement, student loan, tax, insurance, currency, crypto, stock, cloud cost, and similar calculators depend on assumptions you enter and on simplified formulas or reference data. They do not know your full financial situation, tax filing status, credit profile, lender terms, insurance underwriting, local law, transaction fees, market timing, inflation exposure, or risk tolerance.

No finance page on MC NovaTools is financial advice, investment advice, tax advice, legal advice, accounting advice, lending advice, or insurance advice. Do not make a purchase, sale, loan, refinance, tax filing, investment, insurance, or retirement decision solely from a tool result. Compare outputs with official documents and consult qualified professionals.

Finance examples are especially sensitive because small changes in assumptions can create large changes in conclusions. A mortgage refinance estimate can change with closing costs and time horizon; a retirement projection can change with inflation and contribution timing; a crypto tax estimate can change with jurisdiction, lot selection, and transaction history; and a cloud-cost estimate can change with usage spikes, discounts, and provider pricing updates. Results may vary, and the person using the result must verify the assumptions.

sections.title: General tool accuracy disclaimer
body: MC NovaTools provides browser-based utilities and written guides for practical preparation work. The tools can help merge, split, inspect, format, convert, calculate, compress, rename, compare, and organize information, but they cannot guarantee that every input is complete, every file is valid, every assumption is correct, or every output is suitable for a final decision. Results may vary by browser, device memory, file structure, encoding, locale, third-party library behavior, user settings, and the quality of the original source.

Always keep the original file or source data. Review page order, formatting, metadata, units, dates, filenames, special characters, rounding, and edge-case warnings before using an output. If a result affects money, taxes, legal obligations, compliance, accessibility, security, publishing, client delivery, or official records, obtain a qualified human review.

A tool may appear to complete successfully while still requiring review. For example, a PDF merge can preserve pages but not the business meaning of their order; an image compressor can reduce size but damage text legibility; a JSON formatter can make syntax readable without proving the API response is semantically correct; and a text converter can change characters in ways that matter for legal names, product codes, or URLs. Treat the output as prepared material, not automatic approval.

sections.title: Finance and calculator disclaimers
body: Finance calculators on MC NovaTools are educational estimation tools. Mortgage, refinance, compound interest, retirement, student loan, tax, insurance, currency, crypto, stock, cloud cost, and similar calculators depend on assumptions you enter and on simplified formulas or reference data. They do not know your full financial situation, tax filing status, credit profile, lender terms, insurance underwriting, local law, transaction fees, market timing, inflation exposure, or risk tolerance.

No finance page on MC NovaTools is financial advice, investment advice, tax advice, legal advice, accounting advice, lending advice, or insurance advice. Do not make a purchase, sale, loan, refinance, tax filing, investment, insurance, or retirement decision solely from a tool result. Compare outputs with official documents and consult qualified professionals.

Finance examples are especially sensitive because small changes in assumptions can create large changes in conclusions. A mortgage refinance estimate can change with closing costs and time horizon; a retirement projection can change with inflation and contribution timing; a crypto tax estimate can change with jurisdiction, lot selection, and transaction history; and a cloud-cost estimate can change with usage spikes, discounts, and provider pricing updates. Results may vary, and the person using the result must verify the assumptions.

sections.title: Browser processing and privacy limits

Your browser, extensions, operating system, downloads folder, clipboard, localStorage, cache, and network environment can still affect privacy. Avoid using shared computers for sensitive work unless you can clear data afterward.

Those providers operate under their own terms and privacy practices. The Privacy Policy explains Google AdSense, Google Analytics, cookies, and localStorage in more detail.

Always keep the original file or source data. Review page order, formatting, metadata, units, dates, filenames, special characters, rounding, and edge-case warnings before using an output. If a result affects money, taxes, legal obligations, compliance, accessibility, security, publishing, client delivery, or official records, obtain a qualified human review.

A tool may appear to complete successfully while still requiring review. For example, a PDF merge can preserve pages but not the business meaning of their order; an image compressor can reduce size but damage text legibility; a JSON formatter can make syntax readable without proving the API response is semantically correct; and a text converter can change characters in ways that matter for legal names, product codes, or URLs. Treat the output as prepared material, not automatic approval.

Finance examples are especially sensitive because small changes in assumptions can create large changes in conclusions.
